# LunarDyson

> Execution runtime for untrusted Luau programs that orchestrate tools.

A host (any language) hands LunarDyson a small program, usually generated by an LLM. The program runs in a sandboxed Luau VM and can reach the outside world only through the tools the host registered, each with its own budgets. It replaces `LLM → tool → LLM → tool` loops with one generated program that the VM executes deterministically.

## Key properties

- Default deny: no os, io, debug, require, load*, getfenv/setfenv, coroutine; an unregistered tool does not exist
- Static checks: `ld_check` type-checks a program against the registered tool signatures (Luau analyzer, strict or nonstrict) before it runs
- Budgets: memory (allocator), VM time (watchdog + interrupt), calls and response bytes per tool, calls per effect class (pure, read, write, external_write, money); violations are sticky, pcall cannot swallow them
- Step API: execution stops at every tool call and returns to the host (no callbacks across the ABI); each call has a sequential call_id for journaling and replay
- C ABI of 18 functions; Python (cffi) and Go (cgo) bindings; Luau upstream, pinned, no fork
- Tested by a 32-case language-neutral conformance suite in every binding, under ASan/UBSan/LSan and TSan

## Not guaranteed

- No process isolation yet (in-process runtime); run hostile workloads in a worker process or container
- What tools do (authorization, SSRF checks, idempotency) is the host's responsibility

## Status

v0.1, Apache-2.0. Used in production as the script runtime of RiteSmith (https://ritesmith.run).
